title: Count-controlled iteration: the for loop
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Count-controlled loops
objectives: know how to write a for loop that repeats a block a set number of times
understand how range() decides which values the loop counter takes
know how to build a running total inside a loop, and how to put one loop inside another
starter: Write down every number printed by for i in range(2, 9, 3), then say how many lines of output there are altogether.

stations.name: Repeating a line
stations.fact: Iteration is the proper name for repetition, and it is one of the three basic program structures.
stations.challenge: How would you repeat an announcement as many times as the user asks for?

stations.fact: Counting from 0 is normal in programming, and it is why the first item of a list is item 0.

stations.name: Choosing the range
stations.fact: A range does not build a list of its numbers: it works each one out as the loop asks for it.
stations.challenge: Which range lists the hall rows from 4 to 9 inclusive?

stations.name: Running totals
stations.fact: A counter and a running total work the same way: one adds 1, the other adds a value.
stations.challenge: Where must a running total be set to zero, and why there?

stations.fact: Two nested loops of 10 run 100 times, so nesting multiplies the work rather than adding to it.
